correctness.rationale: PASS applies to the corrected RESULT.md, not to the frozen literal opening 'fix one formula A'. The latter is false if it claims the same order for every preselected formula: taking A=p→p excludes both n and f and makes the n- and f-essences designated everywhere. The repair explicitly quantifies uniformly over common arguments, equivalently over a common atom with unrestricted valuations. The designated clauses agree with Petrukhin. The corrected proof identifies the twelve accidents with distinct cut predicates L_K(a,S)=(a in K and S meets K^c) and the essences with their Boolean complements. For distinct cuts neither accident inclusion holds (a two-status witness suffices), and essences never entail accidents because all singleton profiles distinguish those types. An accident entails an essence exactly for disjoint cuts, giving 20+10+10 covers. The 144 essence-to-accident failures are the singleton failures. Size-three failures correspond to intersecting cuts whose union is full, equivalently disjoint cut pairs with proper union by complementation; there are 40−12=28 of these. This leaves 340 size-two failures. All 32 profiles are genuinely realizable by an atom and the number of worlds needed for a profile is its support size. The independent direct-clause enumeration also obtained the exact signatures, comparisons and witness histogram.
residual_risks: The common argument must range uniformly, or be an atom that realizes all profiles. Fixed special formulas can have smaller orders. No claim about preservation of the falsity coordinate, derivability or other accessibility relations.

value.rationale: This is a complete order and minimum-model classification for all bare essence and accident primitives of a published four-valued semantics, not a test of an arbitrary subset. A single disjointness rule explains why the entailment relation has only two levels, and the shared-versus-separate witness criterion gives the exact refutation cutoff and identifies when two worlds are inadequate. This is useful to anyone replacing operators under designated consequence or testing small countermodels; it is not claimed as a new general normal form.
residual_risks: Applicability is deliberately limited to the designated common-argument schema; it is not a classification of general formulas or different arguments.
